title: N-Queens Problem
description: Learn how Backtracking solves constraint-based placement problems using systematic search and pruning.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The N-Queens Problem is one of the most famous Backtracking problems in computer science.

The objective is to place queens on a chessboard so that no queen attacks another.

This problem demonstrates how Backtracking systematically explores valid placements while rejecting impossible configurations early.

sections.title: Understanding the N-Queens Problem
sections.content:
Queens in chess can attack horizontally, vertically, and diagonally.

The challenge is to place N queens on an N × N chessboard while ensuring that no two queens threaten each other.

As board size increases, the number of possible arrangements grows rapidly.

sections.title: Constraint Validation
sections.content:
During exploration, the algorithm checks whether a queen placement violates any constraints.

If two queens attack each other, the current arrangement becomes invalid.

The algorithm immediately abandons invalid configurations and backtracks to try different placements.

sections.title: Systematic Recursive Exploration
sections.content:
The algorithm places queens row-by-row.

For each row, it attempts every valid column position.

If no valid placement exists, the algorithm removes previously placed queens and revisits earlier decisions until a valid arrangement is discovered.

sections.title: Why Backtracking is Effective
sections.content:
Backtracking reduces unnecessary exploration by rejecting invalid states immediately.

Instead of evaluating every possible chessboard arrangement completely, the algorithm prunes impossible branches early.

This significantly improves efficiency compared to brute force enumeration.

sections.title: Constraint Problems in Real Systems
sections.content:
Constraint satisfaction problems appear in scheduling systems, resource allocation, robotics, artificial intelligence, and network configuration.

Many optimization systems rely on Backtracking to search for valid configurations efficiently.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: The N-Queens Problem demonstrates how Backtracking solves constraint-based placement challenges efficiently through recursive exploration, rollback, and pruning of invalid configurations.
